name: MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.CAR.tracialRepresentation_injective
title: Faithfulness of the target-state GNS representation

content.display_title: Faithfulness of the target-state GNS representation
content.one_sentence_role: The ideal dichotomy of the same target forces the constructed nonzero representation to be injective.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $A$ be the completed CAR algebra and $\tau$ its normalized trace. Fix a representative shell family and its chosen unitary links $L_j$ in the selected atomic representation $\pi$. Write $T=C^*(\pi(A),\{L_j\})$ for the resulting concrete target and $\iota:A\to T$, $\iota(a)=\pi(a)$, for its faithful unital source map. This fixes one target and one source map throughout. Choose the state extension $\phi:T\to\mathbb C$ of $\tau$ supplied by state extension along $\iota$. Its GNS representation is $(H_\phi,\rho_\phi,\xi_\phi)$, with

$$\|\xi_\phi\|=1,\qquad \phi(t)=\langle\xi_\phi,\rho_\phi(t)\xi_\phi\rangle.$$

The inner product is linear in its second argument. The $T$-orbit of $\xi_\phi$ is dense by the GNS construction. The representation $\rho_\phi:T\to B(H_\phi)$ is injective.
content.assumptions: The representative shell family is fixed. The established closed two-sided ideal dichotomy of this same $T$ is available as a theorem. The GNS space is nonzero because its canonical vector has norm $1$.
content.conclusion: If $\rho_\phi(t)=\rho_\phi(s)$, then $t=s$. Thus the GNS representation of the chosen state on $T$ is faithful as an algebra representation.
content.proof_summary: Apply the closed-ideal dichotomy to the kernel and exclude the whole-algebra case using the unit on the nonzero GNS space.

proof_steps.text: The kernel $I=\ker\rho_\phi$ is a norm-closed two-sided ideal. The previously established result `shellFamilyTarget_closedIdeal_dichotomy` gives $I=\{0\}$ or $I=T$.

If $I=T$, then $\rho_\phi(1)=0$. But $\rho_\phi$ is unital, so

$$\xi_\phi=I_{H_\phi}\xi_\phi=\rho_\phi(1)\xi_\phi=0,$$

contradicting $\|\xi_\phi\|=1$. Hence $I=\{0\}$, which is precisely injectivity. The source applies `Representation.injective_of_closed_ideal_dichotomy` after installing the separately proved nontriviality of $H_\phi$.

content.lean_realization_notes: This does not infer faithfulness of an arbitrary vector state from faithfulness of its representation. State faithfulness requires its own argument. No irreducibility of $\rho_\phi$, purity of $\phi$, or separability of $T$ is assumed.
